dedupe_keys.name: netherlands red cross 510 ai building footprints for southern guatemala hurricanes eta and iota response

description: The Netherlands Red Cross data team 510 produced these building footprints for southern Guatemala in November 2020 to support the disaster response team during hurricanes Eta and Iota. They are deep-learning predictions on Bing Maps imagery from about 2016 to 2019, made with 510's open automated-building-detection tool, which maps large areas quickly for disaster response from very high resolution imagery of 0.5 metres per pixel or finer and returns buildings as GeoJSON; the tool builds on robosat and robosat.pink. Coverage: southern Guatemala. Access: one GeoJSON file on HDX in WGS 84, with the model code on GitHub. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: the provider warns that buildings may be missing and asks users to complement the data, and the imagery predates the 2020 hurricanes by one to four years. Simulation uses are a building exposure layer where OpenStreetMap coverage is thin, for flood and wind impact estimates and response planning. Related records: Google Open Buildings, Microsoft building footprints and the 510 typhoon priority index.
